title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
gist: Apple unveiled the Watch Series 12 ($399) and Ultra 4 ($799) with a new S11 chip and 'Health Sensing System' that Apple claims delivers the most accurate heart rate sensing of any wearable, including HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequent than prior models, a new 0-10 daily 'readiness' score, and paid access to over 50 biomarker lab tests for $119 through roughly 2,000 US Quest Diagnostics locations.

insights.claim: Apple's new Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 use a redesigned 'Health Sensing System' with ring-organized photodiodes and a larger electrode surface, paired with a new S11 chip, to take heart rate measurements every five seconds and HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequently than prior Apple Watch models.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A 24x increase in HRV sampling frequency is a substantial sensor-fidelity jump that could meaningfully improve Apple's competitive position in the consumer health-wearable and digital-biomarker space against Whoop, Oura, and Garmin.
insights.locator: The new watches can take HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequently

insights.claim: Apple claims the Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 offer the most accurate heart rate sensing in any wearable, based on an internal study on a diverse population of over 1,000 participants.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This is a self-reported, non-independently-verified accuracy claim; worth treating as a marketing data point pending independent validation rather than settled fact.
insights.locator: Apple claims that the new wearables have the most accurate heart rate sensing

themes.theme: New health scoring and clinical lab integration

insights.claim: Apple is introducing a 0-10 'readiness' score that analyzes recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score to indicate daily capacity, updating throughout the day, alongside a forthcoming 'Health Age' score in the iOS Health app later this year.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Composite daily-readiness scoring pushes Apple further into the same product category as Whoop and Oura, intensifying competition in the fitness-wearable software layer rather than just hardware sensors.
insights.locator: the new Watches will also introduce “readiness” scores

insights.claim: Apple's Health app will let users schedule and purchase lab tests covering over 50 key biomarkers for $119 directly through the app at approximately 2,000 Quest Diagnostics locations in the US.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This is a direct commercial integration between Apple's software ecosystem and a major US clinical lab network, a concrete new revenue/data channel worth tracking for both companies and for how it affects consumer diagnostic-testing habits.
insights.locator: Users will be able to schedule and purchase new labs

insights.claim: Apple's Health app will add movement evaluations measuring flexibility, strength, and balance using vision-based AI models on iPhone combined with Apple Watch heart rate data.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Extends Apple Intelligence-style on-device AI beyond text/vision assistants into biomechanical/fitness assessment, a new applied use case for Apple's vision AI models.
insights.locator: The Health app also includes movement evaluations

insights.claim: The Apple Watch Series 12 starts at $399 and the Ultra 4 starts at $799, both available for preorder immediately and shipping September 18; the aluminum Series 12 models are claimed to be 60 percent tougher than prior aluminum models.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Pricing held flat versus recent generations while adding meaningful sensor upgrades suggests Apple is prioritizing feature differentiation over price increases this cycle to sustain Watch upgrade demand.
insights.locator: Both watches are available for preorder today
